newsitem.title: USA: Deere Q4 sales to dealers rise.
newsitem.headline: Deere Q4 sales to dealers rise.

text.p: Deere & Co said Tuesday net sales to dealers of agricultural, industrial and commercial, and consumer equipment totaled $2.49 billion in the fourth quarter, up from $2.34 billion a year ago.
For the fiscal year ended October 31, Deere's net sales to dealers rose to $9.64 billion from $8.83 billion.

Export sales from the United States totaled $1.58 billion, up 20 percent from $1.31 billion last year. Overseas sales for the year gained 26 percent to $2.75 billion from $2.18 billion, and topped $2.5 billion for the first time, Deere said.

Deere's total net sales and revenues for the fourth quarter rose seven percent to $2.92 billion from $2.72 billion. For year, total net sales and revenues gained to nine percent to $11.23 billion from $10.29 billion.

Earlier, Deere reported record fourth quarter income of $174 million or $0.68 a share, up from $151 million or $0.57 a share. For the full year, it earned a record $817 million or $3.14 a share, up from $706 million or $2.71 a share.
Results in 1996 were reduced by a $15.0 million after-tax write-off related to its Mexican operations.

The company's worldwide equipment operations had record net income of $123.4 million in the fourth quarter and $610.0 million for the full year, up from $106.3 million in the 1995 fourth quarter and $529.0 million in the full year.

Worldwide agricultural equipment operating profits in 1996 were $202 million for the quarter and $821 million for the year compared, up from $135 million in the 1995 fourth quarter and $643 million for last year.

Industrial equipment operating profit fell to $34 million for the fourth quarter from $36 million last year, and to $186 million for the year from $198 million. It cited increased development expenses associated with improving the fuel efficiency and emissions performance of new engines.

Worldwide commercial and consumer equipment operating profits fell to $1 million for the quarter from $35 million last year, and to $118 million for 1996 from $165 million a year ago. Deere cited lower sales volume and increased promotional and growth expenditures for the drop.

Net income of the financial services subsidiaries was $47.6 million for the quarter and $196.8 million for the entire year, a gain from $41.0 million in the 1995 fourth quarter and $166.6 million for the year.
